invariant: Every USymbolCloud segment constructs CoordinateChange, whose length is XPoint2D.distance: Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy). That exact rounded length controls both unit vectors and the integer bubble count. Bubble count controls how many java.util.Random values are consumed before later segments and Bezier controls, so a last-bit distance difference at an integer boundary changes the complete deterministic path.
causal_divergence: Rust ports the same seeded random process but computes segment lengths with f64::hypot. Hypot is numerically stronger but not operation-equivalent to Java's multiply-add-then-sqrt expression. For the valid 171 by 99 filled cloud cluster, one segment lands on a bubble-count boundary: Rust consumes a different random sequence and emits a different path while the cluster rectangle, title, members, links, and canvas are exact.
planned_change: Use (dx * dx + dy * dy).sqrt() everywhere the cloud port mirrors CoordinateChange.getLength, preserving Java's operation order for unit vectors, bubble counts, and curve controls. Keep hypot elsewhere unless the Java provenance independently requires this arithmetic. Add threshold-adjacent cloud dimensions and both simple/complex cloud branches to held-out validation.
